results: 1. walking backward: the slow, guarded, wide-based pattern PERSISTS
2. running: cannot run; the pattern does not normalise
3. gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards): no change - the gait is not distractible
4. muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): genuine axial and lower-limb rigidity on passive movement
5. trial of benzodiazepine (diazepam): clear improvement in stiffness and in the gait
6. anti-GAD65 antibodies: MARKEDLY ELEVATED (high-titre, typically >2000 U/mL) - diagnostic in this clinical context
7. needle EMG (continuous motor unit activity at rest): CONTINUOUS motor unit activity at rest in agonist and antagonist simultaneously, abolished by diazepam
